title: A Colony for the Echo Anew
premise: Mirabel Whitlock has spent eleven years alone tending the Svalbard-2 seed vault and the cryo-bay of a colony ship that never launched, recording daily logs for a world that stopped listening. When gravity stutters across the solar system for nine seconds, she realizes someone out there is still running experiments—and that her vault's power draw is the only thing keeping half a million sleepers alive. A salvage crew arrives claiming legal authority over the colony's assets, forcing Mirabel to choose between obeying a law that abandoned her and an inheritance claim filed by the colonists' own descendants. In the end, Mirabel wakes neither faction's chosen half but the children—every sleeper under sixteen—and broadcasts their first breaths to a system that must finally decide what it owes its forgotten.
about_author: Wendell Dunmore is the pen name of a former agricultural archivist who spent a decade cataloguing heirloom seeds before turning to fiction. Writing from a converted grain silo in rural Manitoba, Dunmore crafts quiet, humane science fiction about people who keep things running after everyone else leaves.

chapters.title: The Long Inventory
chapters.summary: Mirabel records her 4,017th daily log, walking the frozen corridors of the seed vault and the darkened cryo-bay, speaking aloud to sleepers who cannot hear. Her routine is interrupted by a power fluctuation she can't explain. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: loneliness worn smooth into ritual, with the first hairline crack of unease.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Gravity fails across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; tools float, seeds drift, and Mirabel clings to a railing watching her whole world lift off the floor. When weight returns, every clock on the station reads identically wrong. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread—the universe just announced it is watching.

chapters.title: Signals in the Ice
chapters.summary: Mirabel digs through archived colony records to find what could cause a system-wide gravity pulse, discovering a redacted project called ECHO ANEW buried in the founder's files. She also finds her own name on a crew manifest she never signed. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery shadowed by the sense that her life was designed, not chosen.

chapters.title: What the Vault Was For
chapters.summary: In flashbacks woven through her log entries, we learn the colony ship Meridian was meant to carry 500,000 sleepers to Proxima; the launch failed, the funding died, and Mirabel volunteered to stay behind as caretaker. The gravity pulse drained three percent of the cryo-bay's reserves. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: grief for a future postponed so long it became a museum.

chapters.title: The Ship That Answers
chapters.summary: A vessel broadcasting no registry transponder decelerates into orbit above the vault. Mirabel hails it repeatedly; it answers only once, with her own voice, replayed from her logs. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: terror and a shameful flicker of hope—someone came, even if they came for the wrong reasons.

chapters.title: Board of Inquiry
chapters.summary: Six salvagers dock: led by Administrator Corven Ashe, who presents a court order declaring the colony's assets forfeit to creditors. His junior officer, Tamsin Okafor, lingers at the cryo-bay window too long. POV: alternating Mirabel and Tamsin. Emotional beat: cold bureaucratic menace meeting a conscience not yet committed.

chapters.title: Property
chapters.summary: Ashe inventory-strips the vault, treating sleeping humans as cargo tonnage. Mirabel stalls him with procedural sabotage while secretly copying the ECHO ANEW files to a handheld drive. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: righteous anger learning patience—the caretaker becomes a saboteur.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Tamsin runs the numbers on waking 500,000 people with the remaining power and finds it impossible; she begins quietly questioning which lives the law values. She and Mirabel share a guarded meal among the seed racks. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: the slow thaw of complicity into doubt.

chapters.title: The Founder's Voice
chapters.summary: The copied files unlock a video testament from colony founder Dr. Ilsa Reyes-Mbeki, revealing ECHO ANEW was a gravity-manipulation experiment gone rogue—an automated system still pulsing, still drawing power, still waiting for instructions no one ever sent. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden—the dead left her a machine, not a choice.

chapters.title: Nine Again
chapters.summary: A second gravity pulse hits, longer this time, cracking a coolant line in the cryo-bay. In the chaos, one sleeper pod fails entirely: a woman named Ada, whose death certificate Mirabel must now write. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: the abstract stakes become a single unbearable face.

chapters.title: Jurisdiction of the Dead
chapters.summary: Ashe uses Ada's death to justify immediate asset liquidation; Tamsin discovers his creditor backers plan to cannibalize the cryo-pods for their fusion cores. She confronts him privately and is threatened with mutiny charges. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: the moment loyalty to a person becomes betrayal of a system.

chapters.title: Descendants
chapters.summary: Mirabel decrypts the colony's original passenger registry and finds living descendants of the sleepers—children of early defectors who settled Mars—still filing annual inheritance claims nobody processes. She sends them a message for the first time in eleven years. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: hope rekindled through kinship; she is not the only one who remembers.

chapters.title: The Claimant
chapters.summary: A ragtag descendant delegation arrives aboard a retrofitted freighter, led by Ada's grandson, Jonah Voss—who bears the dead woman's face. They present a legal counterclaim to the colony itself. Ashe refuses to recognize it. POV: alternating Jonah and Mirabel. Emotional beat: fragile alliance forged between strangers bound by the same sleepers.

chapters.title: Standoff in the Seed Racks
chapters.summary: Ashe's crew moves to seize the cryo-bay; Mirabel locks down the vault using the founder's backdoor protocols, trapping both factions inside a station now losing power faster than anyone planned. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: defiance with a countdown attached—her stand may kill everyone she's protecting.

chapters.title: Negotiating with Gravity
chapters.summary: Studying ECHO ANEW's control schema, Mirabel realizes the pulses aren't malfunctions but requests—a machine asking permission to reroute power. Someone or something wants the sleepers woken and is offering the energy to do it. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: vertigo of scale—the forgotten have been heard all along.

chapters.title: Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: The central dilemma crystallizes: there is power to wake only half the sleepers. Ashe argues for skilled adults; Jonah for elders carrying cultural memory; Tamsin, breaking ranks, proposes the children. The debate tears the alliance apart. POV: rotating Mirabel, Tamsin, Jonah. Emotional beat: the horror of triage dressed up as ethics.

chapters.title: Ashe's Confession
chapters.summary: Cornered by failing systems and Tamsin's evidence, Ashe admits his order was always a cover: his backers want the pods' cores for a private generation ship, and the sleepers were never meant to wake at all. He offers Mirabel a berth to look away. POV: Ashe. Emotional beat: villainy revealed as cowardice—he too is following orders he hates.

chapters.title: The Vote of the Living
chapters.summary: Mirabel does the unthinkable: she puts the question to everyone on the station, salvagers included—one person, one vote, no rank. The children win, narrowly, and Ashe's own crew votes against him. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, improvised in a freezing room, imperfect and real.

chapters.title: Answering the Echo
chapters.summary: Mirabel sends the authorization signal ECHO ANEW has waited decades to receive; the system-wide pulses synchronize and begin channeling stellar-grid power toward the vault. Ashe attempts to jam the transmission and is stopped—not by force, but by his own crew standing down. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: climax—the machine and the caretaker finally speak the same language.

chapters.title: First Breath
chapters.summary: The children's pods open in waves over thirty-six hours. Jonah meets his grandmother's pod-mates; Tamsin resigns her commission mid-broadcast; the first child awake asks Mirabel if the world outside is kind. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: overwhelming tenderness after relentless tension—the payoff of every sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Reckoning Broadcast
chapters.summary: With the children awake and the evidence public, Mirabel transmits the full record—logs, Ashe's confession, the vote—to every inhabited station in the system, daring the law to un-wake what it now must answer for. Ashe surrenders himself to his crew for return and trial. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: vindication without triumph; accountability as the beginning, not the end.

chapters.title: A Colony for the Echo Anew
chapters.summary: One year later, the vault is a school. The adult sleepers remain frozen until the grid can hold them, but the children tend the seed racks, and ships arrive monthly with volunteers. Mirabel records her final log and hands the microphone to a ten-year-old. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: resolution as succession—inheritance fulfilled not by keeping, but by giving away.
